crime: With charcoal from the fireplace, one prisoner kept the name of every living girl on her cell wall, so that no girl who vanished would be forgotten. Each evening {WITCH_NAME} came to read the names, looking for her own.

One evening during free time, after the other visitors had laughed, the girl showed her what was drawn where her name should be: a charcoal lizard. "You're in every crowd," she said, "so you get a lizard."
In her school yearbook, {WITCH_NAME} had stood at the edge of five club photos, and every caption had ended with "and friend."

One night, just before the cells locked at ten, the others in the cell corridor watched her fade into the wall of the cell she had to herself, as she did every night. Still matching every wall she passed, she walked unseen into the other girl's cell and stood in the corner by the bars.

After lockup, the girl wrote something on the wall by her pillow. In that dim light, {WITCH_NAME} could not read it from the corner. Then the girl whispered every name on the wall, ending with "our chameleon."
{WITCH_NAME} pressed her hand over the mouth that had named everyone and held it there until the girl was still. Then she sat against the wall beside her until morning, her back to the names.
When the cells were unlocked, she slipped unseen into the cell corridor while the girl's roommate screamed, then stepped out of her own cell into the crowd.

In the trial court, the prisoners accused the roommate, the only girl who had been locked in with the dead girl. Then one prisoner pointed at the backward charcoal letters smudged across {WITCH_NAME}'s back. They spelled her own name, rubbed off the wall from beside the lizard. The prisoners understood: she had leaned against that wall inside the locked cell.
fields.epitaph: Her name was written at last, and she carried it on her back, the one place she could never read it.
execution: The execution stand opened a giant iron book, and she was strapped flat on its blank left page. By reflex, she faded into the blank page. The facing iron leaf swung up on the spine. Raised on it in iron letters was her name, the only name on the page. The leaf slammed shut over her. The iron book lay shut and still, her name pressed onto the blank she had become.

magic.name: Wallflower
magic.text: Her body, clothes and whatever she carries take on the colors and patterns behind her.
